entries.title: Agent Runtime update: process-str-replace

ai.title: Agent runtime enforces unique fuzzy matches and adds line hints on
ai.summary: The `str_replace` tool in `packages/agent-runtime` now rejects fuzzy matches (extra indentation or whitespace-insensitive) that fit more than one location when `allowMultiple` is false, preserving the uniqueness guarantee of exact matches. On a complete miss, the error message appends a closest-match hint listing file lines that best fit the old string, bounded by `HINT_MAX_LINES`, `HINT_MAX_CHARS`, and `HINT_MIN_KEY_CHARS` constants. This allows the model to correct a near-miss in one retry without re-reading the file or guessing, while a `LOOKALIKE` regex flags curly-quote or non-breaking-space mismatches in the hint.
ai.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/process-str-replace.ts`, `tryMatchOldStr` now calls `tryFuzzyMatch` and `closestMatchHint`; the diff adds `count` enforcement to fuzzy matches (refusing if `fuzzy.count > 1` when `allowMultiple` is false) and appends a `closestMatchHint` string to the miss error, with new tests verifying refusal of multi-fit fuzzy matches and presence of line-numbered hints.

eli5.text: When the coding assistant cannot find the exact text you asked it to change, it now checks if the text is similar to lines elsewhere in the file. If it finds multiple similar spots, it refuses to make the edit to avoid accidentally changing the wrong section. If it finds no match at all, it shows you a few nearby lines from the file so you can copy the correct text more easily on your next try. This makes the tool more careful when editing your code and gives you clearer guidance when an edit fails.

entries.title: SDK update: code-search

ai.title: Code search failure messages now blame install only when ripgrep
ai.summary: In `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts`, the default `timeoutSeconds` for ripgrep is increased from 10 to 20 because shorter limits killed valid searches on large repositories. A new exported helper, `ripgrepFailureMessage`, replaces the inline error handling that previously appended installation advice to every ripgrep failure. The helper now includes that advice only when the error code is `ENOENT` and the expected binary path does not exist on the filesystem, preventing models from incorrectly assuming a missing installation when failures are caused by permissions or system load.
ai.evidence: The diff introduces the `ripgrepFailureMessage` function in `sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts` and updates the default `timeoutSeconds` from 10 to 20. The new function checks `code === 'ENOENT' && !fs.existsSync(rgPath)` to conditionally append installation advice, replacing the previous unconditional error message that blamed the vendor binary for all spawn failures.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now waits double the usual time before giving up on a search of your files, so it is less likely to quit on large projects or slow devices. It also checks whether the search tool is actually missing before telling you to install it, meaning it no longer blames a broken installation when the real problem is a busy computer or a permission error. This makes search results more reliable and stops the assistant from sending you down the wrong fix for simple glitches.

entries.title: SDK update: llm

ai.title: SDK continues idle timeouts after output instead of failing
ai.summary: The SDK's stream recovery now treats a 5-minute fetch inactivity timeout occurring after model output has arrived as a recoverable stream interruption, continuing the step from partial output rather than failing the turn. This mechanism wraps the existing recovery classifiers with `idleTimeoutContinuation`, which calls `classifyIdleTimeoutRecovery` ahead of generic transport classification when the `receivedModelOutput` flag is set. The change specifically addresses a scenario where 620 hosted Cloud runs in two days stopped after output had arrived, preventing the turn from ending silently in these cases.
ai.evidence: New export `classifyIdleTimeoutRecovery` in `sdk/src/impl/stream-interruption.ts` and its integration into `promptAiSdkStream` in `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` via the `idleTimeoutContinuation` wrapper.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now continues an interrupted answer instead of stopping it when it receives some text or actions from a model and then goes silent for five minutes. This protects people running AI coding tasks in the cloud who previously saw their work silently stop mid-sentence after the assistant had already started replying. You will notice fewer dead-ends in long tasks where the connection drops, because the assistant picks up where it left off rather than ending the conversation with no result.
